A_P_CSF_controlled.prior_art: EXTENSIVE — adjustable valves, pressure-controlled valves, ICP sensors exist. This is NOT novel.
A_P_CSF_controlled.verdict: NOT NOVEL — baseline technology, not invention

B_P_CSF_plus_P_venous.proposition: Drainage controlled by P_CSF - P_venous differential
B_P_CSF_plus_P_venous.prior_art: CereVasc patents discuss CSF-to-venous pressure gradient. Cache: 3 matches. PatSnap: 0 patents found.
B_P_CSF_plus_P_venous.verdict: POSSIBLY NOVEL — the DIFFERENTIAL is known, but using it for ACTIVE CONTROL may not be taught. Needs passage-level chart.
B_P_CSF_plus_P_venous.key_question: Does any reference teach USING the measured P_CSF-P_venous differential to ACTIVELY ADJUST drainage (not just passively respond to it)?

C_dynamic_venous_compensation.proposition: Dynamic compensation for CHANGING venous pressure (posture, respiration, Valsalva)
C_dynamic_venous_compensation.prior_art: Anti-siphon devices exist (passive). Programmable valves exist (manually adjusted). But DYNAMIC, AUTOMATIC compensation for venous pressure CHANGES is not known.
C_dynamic_venous_compensation.verdict: LIKELY NOVEL — passive anti-siphon is known, but active venous-pressure compensation is different
C_dynamic_venous_compensation.key_question: Does any reference teach automatic, real-time adjustment of drainage in response to venous pressure changes?

D_predictive_control.proposition: Predict future venous state changes and pre-adjust drainage
D_predictive_control.prior_art: No known prior art for predictive CSF drainage control.
D_predictive_control.verdict: LIKELY NOVEL — predictive control is a different paradigm from reactive control
D_predictive_control.key_question: Does any reference teach PREDICTING venous pressure changes and pre-adjusting drainage?

E_eShunt_specific_venous_boundary.proposition: Using the venous boundary as BOTH sensor input AND controlled output (the venous system is both what you measure and what you drain into)
E_eShunt_specific_venous_boundary.prior_art: VP shunts cannot do this (peritoneum is not measurable). eShunt-specific by construction.
E_eShunt_specific_venous_boundary.verdict: LIKELY NOVEL — the venous boundary as a dual-purpose (sensor + output) is unique to eShunt
E_eShunt_specific_venous_boundary.key_question: Does any reference teach using the venous drainage boundary as both a pressure sensor input and a drainage output in a closed-loop system?

where_prior_art_stops: Prior art stops at proposition B (differential is known) and does not clearly teach C (dynamic compensation), D (predictive), or E (venous boundary as dual-purpose). The invention territory is in C-D-E, not A-B.
recommended_claim_direction: Focus on C (dynamic venous compensation) and E (venous boundary as dual sensor+output). D (predictive) is the platform play connecting to Position #1.
